sections.value:
**#149 after-deploy: +0 recorded daemon launches/60.002153 s; no owed-notice boot drain observed.**

Reported merge and canonical checkout: **3137c9b9581531a5ed4e9197e2ee5ce9f2521b25**. Daemon **PID 53891**, process start **2026-11-08 02:42:48 +10:00**, unchanged across snapshots; store **user_version 40**. Ping's generic build label is not an embedded Git SHA.

Two pings: **2026-11-08 02:55:58.879522 to 02:56:58.881994 +10:00**, **60.002153 s** monotonic elapsed.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Daemon launches | **159 to 159: +0, 0.000/s**, all 16 populated sites flat |
| Registration counters | **9 attempts / 12 ps**, unchanged |
| Daemon interval CPU | **7.21 CPU seconds / 60.002153 s = 12.02%** of one CPU |
| RSS | **193.59 MiB to 193.59 MiB**, unchanged |
| Machine launches | **18.1/s**, separate niced 20-second sample |
| Closed/owed notices | **0 closed rows and 0 owed rows**; initial notice-state inventory also empty |
| Close FYIs since boot | **0** by request-closed ID metadata |
| Claude window outcomes | **0**, so no second traffic-bearing F82 note |

**Boot distinction:** the source's boot recover_requests handles requests left delivering. Closed owed notices have no automatic boot sweeper here; they are retried by an authorized close command. There was no observed owed backlog or close FYI drain to measure. This does not verify recovery under a pre-existing owed-notice workload.

RSS is higher than the earlier #153 window's 137.81 MiB, but those windows have different daemon incarnations/workloads. Nothing attributes that difference to close-notice retention; the closed table is empty in this reading. Rolling ps CPU (76.7/43.3%) was not used as interval CPU.

The machine sample attributed **18.0/s** as a lower bound: **10.9/s other**, **7.1/s gone before identification**, no observed daemon-child contribution. It made **269,175 in-process polls** in 20 seconds and is CPU work despite nice priority. Its scope differs from the daemon minute.

Metadata was read-only: close/owed counts, FYI IDs/sender/recipient/state/timestamps, and indexed Claude outcome fields. No message bodies, credential files, test/model/synthetic traffic, build or restart.

Raw session receipts: `pr149-after-window.json`, `pr149-after-machine.json`, `pr149-after-notice-before.json`, `pr149-after-notice-evidence.json`. Contended close/drain/notice latency and retention remain unmeasured; F82's traffic-bearing window remains pending.
